gh pr create --base main --head lane/attest-stores-text-356b --title "APRV-356: terminal attestations store the attested policy text, and the ceremony verbs commit it" --body-file - <<'BODY'
Closes APRV-356.

The last phone-attestation residual from APRV-324. Attestation answers are
resolved against the policy IN FORCE, and `inForcePolicyText` could only
recover those bytes for a chain that had been proposed to a phone: a terminal
attestation recorded the digest and stored nothing, so this repository's own
chain had no recoverable bytes at all. The fallback was safe and left one
documented hole: an amendment that REMOVES a sender mapping was
indistinguishable from a policy that never had one.

## What is in it

Two commits.

**`5b1e1d1` — the core** (authored by the previous lane, unchanged here)

- `src/core/attest.ts` stores the attested bytes in the content-addressed
  payload store and binds their hash on the `policy.updated` it appends. A
  store that cannot be written REFUSES the attestation: a record claiming a
  binding whose bytes are absent is a worse artifact than no record.
- `src/core/policy-proposal.ts`: `inForcePolicyText` reads an attestation's own
  binding as readily as a proposal's, re-hashing the recovered text against the
  attested digest from the verified log. The store is checked, never trusted.
- **Schema change:** `schema/event.schema.json` gains an optional, described
  `payload_hash` on the `policy.updated` payload. Additive: records written
  before this validate and verify unchanged, and a reader treats absence as the
  pre-amendment state where the fail-closed fallback applies.
- **SPEC.md 5.2 and 10.4 amended**, and the residual paragraph in
  **`design/channel-sender-identity.md`** rewritten as closed. Both are in that
  one commit and are not touched again on this branch (the guard replay budget
  rule from the 2026-09-18 handover).
- Tests: `sender-identity` case 26 is the closure and fails on the old
  behaviour; 26a pins the bootstrap refusal; 26b pins the fail-closed fallback
  for a chain attested before this change, built through the real append path.
  `prune` pins that retention never takes the in-force policy text.

**`626c4f9` — the behaviour change this PR adds**

`approval policy amend --commit`, `approval policy apply` (which runs an amend)
and `approval log advance` now put the payload file the attestation binds in
the commit they build. The advance already carried `.approval/payloads` whole;
amend and apply carry the one file, beside `APPROVAL.md`, the log and the pins.

This is not a stale-test fix. A committed log carrying a binding without the
bytes is a chain whose in-force policy is unrecoverable to every reader of the
committed copy, which is the state this task exists to end, and the CI
protected-path guard resolves payloads out of committed trees, so that copy is
the one it reads.

- `core/attest.ts` exports `attestedPolicyPayload` / `attestedPolicyPayloadHash`,
  so the `{ text }` store shape has one author and the ceremony can name the
  file the attestation will land in before the append happens.
- `cli/amend.ts` treats the payload path as a ceremony file from the start:
  `--dry-run` names it in the `git add` it would run, and `--commit` counts it
  as its own rather than as a stray in the index. The human path binds the
  attestation's payload; the agent path binds the proposal's, which is what
  carries the text on a chain attested from a phone. The success headline and
  the `staged-unrelated` refusal name all four files.
- `core/policy-proposal.ts`: the unrecoverable-bytes refusal named only
  `policy.proposed`; it now names both kinds of record.
- `docs/cli-reference.md`: the attest payload shape with `payload_hash` and
  why, and step 7 of the amend order.
- The suites that pinned the old path sets and the old store counts move with
  it (amend, log-verbs advance, policy-apply-publish, attest, doctor, status,
  hook prompts, payload-store, render-queue). Where a fixture assumed an empty
  store it now asserts the delta, because an absolute would be a claim about
  the fixture. `cli-style-render` masks the store path before the no-64-hex
  rule: a content-addressed file NAME is a path the operator types exactly,
  never a digest on display.

## Verification

`npm test`: 4694 tests, 4671 pass, **22 fail**, exit 1. All 22 are the
pre-existing Node v26 SMTP/email failures on this laptop (`TLS ServerName may
not be an IP`); none is touched by this PR and CI on Node 22 is the truth.
`npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` clean; `npm run
conformance` 374/374.

No SPEC section 11 invariant is weakened. The store stays content-addressed and
re-verified on every read, so nothing new is trusted; the fail-closed direction
is preserved at the one new decision point (an unwritable store refuses the
attestation rather than appending a binding nobody can resolve).
